name: EMS ab belt

lead: An EMS ab belt is a pad-lined belt that delivers pulses of electric current through the skin over the abdominal muscles, causing them to contract involuntarily. It is sold as a hands-free way to tone and sculpt the midsection.
It appears in looksmaxxing discussions as a shortcut to abs, and is generally dismissed there: contractions are real, but visible abs depend on training and low body fat.

paras: The electrodes depolarize motor nerves under the skin, which triggers contraction in the muscle beneath. Clinical EMS can preserve or modestly increase muscle in people who cannot exercise. Evidence for body-composition change mostly concerns whole-body EMS suits supervised by trainers, not consumer belts, and even there an added benefit over ordinary exercise is small.

Reported problems include skin irritation, burns from poor contact, and interference with pacemakers and other implants, so they are not for people with such devices or pregnancy. Regulators have not cleared consumer ab stimulators for weight loss, girth reduction or defined abs. The claim that a belt produces a six-pack is unsupported; at best it gives modest, temporary toning.
